chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan and Ibn Abi 'Umayr, all from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Talbiyah is: 'Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Indeed praise and grace are Yours and the dominion, You have no partner.' Then he mentioned the hadith until he said: 'And know that the four Talbiyahs which are at the beginning of the report are obligatory, and they are Tawhid (divine unity), and by it the Messengers proclaimed, and increase in Dhi al-Maaraj, for indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to increase in it.'

And we have cited this report in its form previously, and as for Tawaf, we have also clarified its obligation in what preceded, and that the Mufrid is required to perform two Tawafs and one Sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and likewise the Qarin and the Mutamatti' are required to perform three Tawafs and two Sa'is between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and there is sufficiency in it, if Allah wills, and that is also confirmed by what was narrated:

key_terms.اَلتَّلْبِيَةُ: The Talbiyah, the specific proclamation 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' recited during Hajj
key_terms.اَلتَّوْحِيدُ: Tawhid, the concept of divine unity, identified here as the core meaning of the Talbiyah
key_terms.اَلسَّعْيُ: Sa'i, the ritual walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah
key_terms.اَلطَّوَافُ: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.اَلْقَارِنُ: Al-Qarin, a pilgrim who combines Hajj and Umrah together
key_terms.اَلْمُتَمَتِّعُ: Al-Mutamatti', a pilgrim who performs Umrah first and then Hajj
key_terms.اَلْمُفْرِدُ: Al-Mufrid, a pilgrim who performs Hajj only (without Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific ritual requirements for Tawaf and Sa'i for different types of Hajj pilgrims according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the Talbiyah as the fundamental expression of Tawhid, linking the pilgrim's response directly to the tradition of the Prophets. The narration further clarifies the jurisprudential distinctions among Hajj types, specifying that while the Mufrid performs one Tawaf and one Sa'i, both the Qarin and Mutamatti' are required to perform three Tawafat and two Saiys, reflecting the cumulative nature of their rituals.
